questions.question: For carbohydrates, proteins and fats, give one function, one South African food source and the food test with its positive result.
questions.expected_answer: Carbohydrates: main energy source; e.g. maize meal, rice, bread; starch test with iodine, yellow-brown to blue-black (glucose: Benedict's, heated, blue to orange or brick-red). Proteins: growth and repair, enzymes and antibodies; e.g. beans, eggs, pilchards, amasi; Biuret test, blue to purple. Fats: concentrated energy store, insulation, cell membranes; e.g. cooking oil, nuts, avocado; grease-spot test, translucent spot on paper.

questions.question: Calculate the energy in a food containing 40 g carbohydrate, 6 g protein and 8 g fat, using 17 kJ/g for carbohydrate and protein and 37 kJ/g for fat.
questions.expected_answer: Carbohydrate: 40 × 17 = 680 kJ. Protein: 6 × 17 = 102 kJ. Fat: 8 × 37 = 296 kJ. Total: 680 + 102 + 296 = 1078 kJ.

questions.question: Distinguish between kwashiorkor and marasmus and name the deficiency diseases caused by a lack of vitamin C, iron and iodine.
questions.expected_answer: Kwashiorkor is caused by a severe lack of protein (often on a mainly starchy diet) and shows a swollen belly and legs from fluid, thin arms, peeling skin and thin, discoloured hair. Marasmus is caused by a lack of both energy and protein (starvation) and the child is extremely thin, skin and bone. Vitamin C: scurvy. Iron: anaemia. Iodine: goitre.
